body:
## Serial behind #12394 — recorded, with the measurement triage asked for

Triage on #12394 flagged fold-or-serial as the seat's call. Answered by measuring both bands in the one file they share, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/seed-tenancy-backfill.ts` (1171 lines on `origin/main`):

| card | symbols | lines |
|---|---|---|
| **#12395** (this) | the `organizationIds.length !== 1` guard and its warning payload | `1016–1025` |
| **#12394** (mechanism) | `buildCounterMergeSql` / `buildGlobalCounterDeleteSql` / `buildOrgCounterProbeSql` + call sites | `639`, `652`, `661`, loop at `1091–1118` |

Textually disjoint, 66 clear lines between them — so the ruling is **not** a merge-conflict argument, and the region-by-symbol test would have allowed parallel work. It is serial on a **semantic** dependency instead:

This card's own proposed remedy is a third state that stays silent (or drops to `info`) when `organizationCount` is 0. **That is precisely the state in which #12394's counter destruction fires.** Implementing the silence first would remove the only signal a fresh install currently emits about a defect that is otherwise invisible on the happy path — the card itself makes that point, that the warning "buried a real defect". So the mechanism gets repaired first, and this diagnostic is then redesigned against a backfill that no longer loses the high-water mark. That also changes what the right answer here *is*: once the merge is atomic, `organizationCount: 0` really is benign, and the silence is defensible rather than a cover-up.

Not folded into #12394 either. The fix shapes are unlike — merge/delete atomicity versus warning semantics and probe ordering — and bundling them would blur each one's ablation, which is exactly the evidence a data-corruption fix cannot afford to have blurred.

Staying in `pm:queue`, unassigned, dispatched as soon as #12394 lands. Problem 2 (the probe running 194 ms into an inline seed, so the object list is a race snapshot rather than a measurement) is untouched by that ordering and remains fully specified as filed.

The #698 attribution correction in the last section is real and is not this seat's to make — it belongs to whoever owns the consumer-repo card. Flagging it rather than acting on it.

## Serial hold released — claimed and dispatched

- **Session**: `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o` (seat post #6367)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-12395-backfill-warning-semantics`
- Comments re-read in the same action as the claim: two — triage's grading and my own serial ruling. No competing claim from any other session.

**#12394 has landed, verified by content on `origin/main` rather than by the API's `merged` field**: `mergeSplitCounter` resolves 3 times in `seed-tenancy-backfill.ts`, with `buildSplitProbeSql` firing twice in the same scan as the positive control. The hold is discharged.

### The ordering did what it was for

The serial ruling was not merge-conflict hygiene — the bands were 66 lines apart and would have passed the region test. It was semantic, and the payoff is that **this card's answer is now different from what it would have been this morning**. The remedy on the table is a third state that stays silent (or drops to `info`) at `organizationCount: 0`. That was the exact state in which #12394's counter destruction fired, so implementing it first would have deleted the only signal a fresh install emitted about a defect invisible on the happy path — the card's own words, that the warning *"buried a real defect"*.

With the merge now atomic and the high-water mark written before anything is retired, `organizationCount: 0` **really is** benign. The silence is defensible on the merged tree in a way it simply was not before, and the dev is told to establish that on the current ref rather than inherit it from me.

### ⚠️ Re-locate everything by symbol — the file moved a long way under this card

Triage's own instruction: *"whichever lands second must re-check the other's diff on the merged ref."* That is not a formality here. #12394 grew `seed-tenancy-backfill.ts` by roughly 200 lines, so **every line number in this card's body and in my earlier comment is now wrong** — including the `1016–1025` band I quoted. `buildOrgCounterProbeSql` was deleted outright by that PR.

I have told the dev in as many words to locate the guard and its warning payload by symbol, and to treat my `1016–1025` as historical. A PR quoting a line number that has moved is a PR nobody can check, and I would rather say that against my own comment than have it discovered.

Problem 2 — the probe running 194 ms into an inline seed, so the named object list is a race snapshot rather than a measurement (3 objects on first boot, 9 on the settled database) — is untouched by all of the above and dispatched as filed.

The hotcrm#698 attribution correction stays flagged and unacted: it belongs to the consumer-repo seat, and triage records it as already on hotcrm#1292's closure trail.
